To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the recognition accuracy can be improved by processing images with recognition loss, which can also be achieved in an unsupervized way, (b) the processing model can be transferred to different recognition models, and (c) the recognition accuracy is more important than image processing quality for the downstream task
We present the first work that improves the interpretability of processed image for machines, and that this can be achieved in an unsup-ervised way.

1) the image processing network can improve the recognition accuracy by optimizing the recognition loss, even if the recognition model is not used as part of the image processing network; and 2) the improvement in recognition accuracy is transferable across different recognition models, which can be applied even if we do not know what the future recognition model will be.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: can we improve machine interpretability by optimizing the image processing pipeline?
the problem of improving the interpretability of images for machine recognition.
the question: how can image processing models be designed to improve machine interpret-ability of images while maintaining or even enhancing human perception?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

\textit{Transferable Recognition-AWARE Image Processing (TRAIP)} is a novel method for image processing that improves the recognition performance of downstream models, even when they are different from the model that was used for training the image processing model.

this work presents a simple and effective approach that enables image processing to enhance the recognition ability of the resulting images, and this ability can transfer to different recognition models.
this work proposes a novel framework for improving the machine interpretability of images by optimizing the recognition loss on the image processing networks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a simple approach to improve machine interpret-ability of processed images.
we can improve the machine interpretability of the processed image by optimizing the recognition loss of the image processing network directly or through an intermediate model.
we show that it is possible to improve the interpretability of processed visual data for machines, while keeping or even improving the quality for human perception.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we can improve image recognition performance by directly optimizing the recognition performance of the images, without requiring any additional annotations or labels, which is a very appealing feature in practice.
image processing can be designed with the goal of improving machine interpretability of the processed image.

image processing models can be made more robust to the recognition models they interact with, and that this robustness transfers between recognition models, making the processed image more robust to the future recognition models as well.
